roadmap.goal: Forecast Reality Check (Epic #4172), slices 01 and 02 only. One press of Run reality check on a Team's Forecast tab replays that Team's own How-Many forecast against its own finished history at every sampling window on the standard ladder [14, 30, 60, 90] plus the Team's own window when it is off that ladder, times the horizons [7, 14, 28, 56] days: sixteen checks, or twenty. Each check ends today and is read at the 50/70/85/95 levels. The answer is one envelope of facts: the region of sampling windows that hold up, never a winner; where the Team's own setting stands; how often each level held against how often it should have; the denominator; and every check, including the ones that could not be evaluated, with the reason. Phase 01 is slice 01 (Story #6072): the endpoint, the pure verdict policy, the read-only and permission guarantees, the card and its sentence on the Forecast tab, the name-only usage-data event TeamForecastRealityCheckRun = 11, one Playwright walking skeleton, and a closing measurement of the production service against the R-1 budget. Phase 02 is slice 02 (Story #6073): the evidence panels, the band rows, the nominal-rate table and the permanent not-comparable note. Slice 03 (Story #6074, Copy as Markdown) is DEFERRED by the maintainer and has no step. Done when: every one of the 78 pending DISTILL definitions (110 executed cases) is un-ignored or un-skipped and green; the one already-green pin The_single_back_test_beside_the_check_still_answers_as_it_did stays green; the backend builds with no new warning and the connector-excluded suite is green; pnpm test and pnpm build are clean; SonarQube Cloud reports no new issue of any severity; no EF migration exists; ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy.cs and the forecast engine are byte-unchanged; and the orchestrator's Stryker run, last and on frozen code, reaches at least 80% on both stacks.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta property-based unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply here, and leaving it out is a decision, not an oversight. This repository is C# .NET 10 + NUnit 4.6 + Moq + WebApplicationFactory + ArchUnitNET on the backend and TypeScript + Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend, with Playwright page objects for E2E. It has no pytest, no pytest-bdd, no .feature file and no Hypothesis, and DISTILL recorded the same reconciliation for this feature. The acceptance scenarios were written by Quinn at DISTILL: 47 backend methods behind [Ignore(Pending)] and 31 frontend definitions behind it.skip / it.skip.each. The crafter authors none of them. RED means removing the [Ignore] or the .skip and watching the named test fail for the reason red-classification.md records: backend 'expected OK, got NotFound' or the throwing query-count seam; frontend 'no Run reality check button'. A test that fails on anything else when un-ignored is a harness problem, and it is fixed before any production edit. GREEN means production code. There are four deliberate exceptions, each named where it applies. (1) The inner-loop unit tests for RealityCheckVerdictPolicy and ForecastRealityCheckService. Stryker.NET excludes the acceptance category, and those two types are its primary targets, so without value-in/value-out NUnit cases the backend kill rate on them would be close to zero. DEVOPS names these tests as the instrument for §4.3. (2) One ForecastService.test.ts case for runRealityCheck, in the same pattern as runBacktest. Every acceptance spec stands that method in, so no other test runs the real one. (3) The test-side seam in RealityCheckQueryCountTest and the [Explicit] probe, both handed to DELIVER by DISTILL. (4) The Playwright walking skeleton and its page object, which DISTILL listed and deliberately left unwritten.

user_decisions: DES-14 (rule A, confirmed by the maintainer) — a sampling window holds up when its 95% forecast held (actual >= value at 95) in MORE than half of the checks that could be evaluated on it. Two short-falls of four put it outside. Delivering more than the 50% forecast never counts against a window. A partly evaluable window is judged on the checks that ran, and a single check that ran decides it alone. A window with no evaluable check is 'not evaluated' and is never in the region. soundWindowDays is sampledWindowDays filtered, in ladder order.

DES-15 — determination, evaluated in this order: NotEnoughEvidence when no window was evaluated; AllWindowsAlike when EVERY sampled window was evaluated and holds up; NoWindowSound when at least one was evaluated and none holds up; SomeWindowsSound otherwise. unevaluatedWindowDays is new; it lists the windows with no evaluable check and never overlaps soundWindowDays.

DES-16 (name confirmed as SometimesHeld) — NotEvaluated when evaluated = 0; NeverHeld when held = 0 and expected >= 1; AlwaysHeld when held = evaluated and evaluated - expected >= 1; SometimesHeld otherwise. The client prints the two counts beside SometimesHeld with no calibration adjective. The words 'about right' appear nowhere.

DES-17 — currentSettingStanding gains NotTested. currentSettingNotTestedReason is UsesFixedDates | NotAPositiveLength | null, and UsesFixedDates wins when both apply. Invariant: currentSettingWasTested == false <=> standing NotTested <=> reason non-null. A Team with no rolling window gets the standard sixteen checks.

DES-18 — the controller reads GetForecastThroughputStatus, as RunBacktest does. The sweep never does. On a cold cache the sweep reads 20 times (standard ladder) or 24 (off-ladder); a whole request reads 21 or 25.

DES-13 — the Team's own positive rolling window is always swept: sampledWindowDays = sort(standardWindowDays ∪ {ThroughputHistory}). That gives 16 cells on the ladder and 20 off it. cells is always complete, and an unevaluable cell is present with forecast, outcome and levelOutcomes all null (P-D3).

DES-1/DES-2/DES-3 — the response carries facts, never a rendered sentence. It has no per-window scalar, no recommended window, no bounds pair and no ladderKind. The client names a span only when the windows that hold up are a contiguous run of sampledWindowDays; otherwise it lists them.
DES-5 / E1 — ForecastRealityCheckService takes the resolved Team as a parameter and holds no repository and no Data type. The feature has no write path. DoD 13.
DES-6 — the band is plain MUI Box layout, each row normalised to its own extent. No charting library and no shared axis.

DEVOPS — TeamForecastRealityCheckRun = 11, appended and never renumbered, carries its name only. It is reported from the browser after runRealityCheck resolves with a result, including an all-unevaluable result and a fixed-dates Team. It is never reported on the press or on a failed request. The backend change lands first.

D6 — no date picker and no dates in the request. D9 — the shipped sufficiency bar is reused unchanged, and ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy.cs stays byte-unchanged. D12 — no CLI/MCP exposure. D8 / DoD 7 — no entity and no EF migration.

phases.name: One sentence about your sampling window, and which numbers held up
phases.description: Story slice 01 (#6072), built outside in. The walking skeleton comes first: the endpoint wired through Program.cs, answering with the complete envelope for a Team on the standard ladder. The pure verdict policy follows, value in and value out: which levels held, the cell outcome, the level readings, rule A for the region, per-check sufficiency, and the determination over the three window states. Then the parts of the answer that hang on the Team itself: the off-ladder fifth window, the not-tested standing, the filter read in the controller and its query count, who may ask, and the ArchUnit rules. Then the card and its sentence on the Forecast tab. Then the usage-data event, backend first. Then one Playwright walking skeleton, and last a measurement of the production service against the R-1 budget.

steps.name: Walking skeleton — the check answers on the Forecast route with a complete envelope for a Team on the standard ladder
steps.description: The thinnest end-to-end slice through the production composition root. POST /api/latest/forecast/reality-check/{teamId}, guarded TeamRead, resolves the Team through the shipped GetEntityByIdAnExecuteAction, maps applyFilterOverride through the shipped MapOverrideToFilterMode, and reads the filter status in the controller. It then hands the Team to a new sweep service. For each (horizon, window) pair the service builds the cell's dates from today, reads that cell's own history window through GetBlackoutAwareThroughputForTeam, reads the actual once per horizon, turns the horizon into working days through the blackout service, runs the shipped HowMany, and reads the four levels. It returns the whole envelope: ladder, horizons, levels, minimumActiveDays echoed, denominator, cells and level outcomes. The pure verdict policy is born here with Held and nothing else.
unskips: [Ignore(Pending)] removed :: Maria_runs_the_reality_check_on_Ocean_Explorer_and_gets_an_answer_without_giving_a_date — the walking skeleton, the one scenario that runs the shipped Monte Carlo
Already green, must STAY green :: The_single_back_test_beside_the_check_still_answers_as_it_did — the coexistence pin. This step is the one most able to break it, because it edits ForecastController.
criteria: Both routes answer, because the two [Route] attributes sit on the controller class. The action carries [RbacGuard(RbacGuardRequirement.TeamRead, ScopeIdRouteKey = "teamId")], byte-identical to RunBacktest, from its first commit. A route never ships unguarded, even for one commit.

The request body has one field, bool? ApplyFilterOverride, and no [JsonRequired] (ci-learnings S6964: a value-type field on a [FromBody] DTO must be opt-in). There are no dates and no input validation. Absent or null means RespectTeamSetting.

The envelope carries EVERY field of the Response Contract from this step on, including unevaluatedWindowDays, currentSettingNotTestedReason and levelCoverage. Fields whose rule lands in a later step are computed by the simplest rule the scenarios of this step allow, and the step that owns the rule replaces it. No field is omitted and no field is added beyond the contract: no recommendedWindow, no per-window scalar, no bounds pair, no sentence.

Each cell's dates are exact: scoredPeriodEnd = anchorDate = the instance's today from ILighthouseClock; scoredPeriodStart = anchorDate − horizonDays; historyWindowEnd = scoredPeriodStart; historyWindowStart = scoredPeriodStart − samplingWindowDays. The feature never reads DateTime.UtcNow or DateTime.Today (E3, CalendarDayAnchorSeamArchUnitTest).
The actual is read once per HORIZON and shared across the windows. It is never read per cell, because 01-10's query count pins 20/24.
A level holds when actualCompleted >= that level's forecast value (ADR-210). RealityCheckVerdictPolicy is a static class with no constructor dependencies. Today and every input arrive as parameters.
The shipped engine is called unchanged. Every existing forecast test and The_single_back_test_beside_the_check_still_answers_as_it_did pass UNEDITED before and after this step.

The constructor width is handled without tripping S107. ForecastController already takes 7 collaborators. Preferred: inject IForecastRealityCheckService into the action with [FromServices], as AuthController.cs:95 does. This keeps the constructor at 7 and leaves the three places that construct the controller untouched (ForecastControllerTest.cs:711, ForecastFilterBacktestIntegrationTest.cs, ForecastFilterTeamForecastIntegrationTest.cs). Fallback: a narrow `#pragma warning disable S107` at the constructor, with a plain-language reason, and those three construction sites updated.
The RED run is captured before any production edit. Every named scenario must fail on 'expected OK, got NotFound', as red-classification.md records.

`dotnet build` introduces no new warning (the six Microsoft.Build 18.10.1 TFM warnings already on main are the only ones allowed), and `dotnet test --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"` is green.

Nothing trips a rule in docs/ci-learnings.md. Before push, run `dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore` over every touched AND new .cs file, taking the union of git diff and git status --porcelain. Watch in particular: CA1861 (hoist the ladder, horizon and level arrays to static readonly fields), CA1859 (private helpers return List<T>/T[]), CS9236, S107, S3776.
steps.implementation_notes: Files: RealityCheckInputDto, RealityCheckResultDto (the envelope and its nested DTO family; split them one type per file if that is the house style), RealityCheckVerdictTypes (the closed sets Determination, CurrentSettingStanding, NotTestedReason, SufficiencyReason, CellOutcome, LevelReading — domain enums, so the policy never depends on API.DTO), IForecastRealityCheckService, ForecastRealityCheckService, RealityCheckVerdictPolicy and ForecastRealityCheckServiceTest are all NEW. ForecastController and Program.cs are edits. Enums serialise as strings outbound, and the scenarios read them as words (P-D2). The ArchUnit rules at 01-12 find these types by name. Anything whose name contains 'RealityCheck' must not reach Services.Interfaces.Repositories or Lighthouse.Backend.Data, and the policy must not reach Services.Implementation apart from ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy. Honour that from this first commit, not at 01-12. The service's contract is a bounded change with an empty mutation set, and it holds no IRepository<Team> (DES-5). ForecastRealityCheckServiceTest is inner-loop: mock the four ports and assert the cell dates, one actual read per horizon, and the envelope's echo fields, because Stryker excludes the acceptance category. Program.cs is on the shared-path list, so the push that lands this step runs the FULL live-connector Integration suite once in CI. Expect it. A red unauthenticated GitHub pair on a rate limit is not this feature's defect. Locally, run only the filtered suite. Comments: if the per-horizon actual read needs a why, say in plain words that the scored period depends only on the horizon. Never cite DES-, ADR-, AC-, D- or E- ids in code comments. They name sections of documents a cold reader cannot open. Commit: `feat(forecast): the reality check answers for a team, one envelope of facts (story 6072)`

steps.name: Each check says where the Team's actual landed against its forecast band
steps.description: The pure cell verdict. Below the 95% value the cell is OverForecast; inside the band from 95% up to 50% it is WithinBand; above the 50% value it is UnderForecast. The four held flags follow from the same actual. The policy decides it and the service copies it into the cell.
unskips: [Ignore(Pending)] removed :: Each_check_says_where_the_Teams_actual_landed_against_its_forecast — 5 cases (NoLevel, NinetyFive, EightyFive, Seventy, EveryLevel)
criteria: The boundaries are inclusive exactly as ADR-210 draws them. Actual equal to the 95% value is WithinBand and holds at 95. Actual equal to the 50% value is WithinBand and holds at every level. Only actual strictly above the 50% value is UnderForecast.
CellOutcome is a pure function of the four forecast values and the actual. It lives in the policy, and the service holds no copy of the rule.
RealityCheckVerdictPolicyTest is NEW and value-in/value-out: [TestCase] rows at, just below and just above each band edge. It uses no database, no host and no simulation.

`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched and new files. No inline array in an NUnit assertion (CA1861) and NUnit4002/NUnit2045 are respected in the new test file.
steps.implementation_notes: If the policy uses a switch expression over one of the closed enums with no discard arm, the build needs a narrow CS8524 pragma with a plain-language reason. CS8509 is still reported without it (a known trap in this codebase). Commit: `feat(forecast): each check says where the actual landed (story 6072)`

steps.name: Each level reports how often it held against how often its own percentage said it should
steps.description: Level coverage over the evaluable checks. heldCount per level, expectedHeldCount = runsEvaluated × P / 100 (ADR-210 — P, never 100 − P), and a reading from DES-16. NeverHeld and AlwaysHeld are findings only when the level's own rate expected at least one whole check to go the other way. Otherwise the reading is SometimesHeld.
criteria: The expected count is evaluated × P / 100. At the 50% level the complement formula gives the same number, which is how that mistake once survived review, so the 70/85/95 rows are the ones that prove it.

The readings follow DES-16 exactly. NotEvaluated when evaluated = 0 (the reading is added now and exercised end to end at 01-07). NeverHeld when held = 0 and expected >= 1. AlwaysHeld when held = evaluated and evaluated − expected >= 1. SometimesHeld otherwise. With 16 checks a 95% level holding in 16 is SometimesHeld (0.8 of a miss expected), while 50/70/85 holding in 16 are AlwaysHeld.
The wire name is SometimesHeld. AboutRight does not exist anywhere in the code.
The policy unit test pins every threshold edge: expected exactly 1.0, just under, just over; held = evaluated with evaluated − expected = 0.99 and 1.0; evaluated = 0.

`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files (compare doubles with a tolerance constraint, never Is.EqualTo on a computed double without .Within).
steps.implementation_notes: DES-16 has the case table: 16 checks held 8/11/14/15 all read SometimesHeld; 12 checks at 95 holding 12 read SometimesHeld. No comment names DES-16. If the one-whole-check threshold needs a why, write it in plain words: the level's own rate predicted fewer than one miss, so never missing is what it predicted. Commit: `feat(forecast): each level held against its own rate (story 6072)`

steps.name: The region of windows that hold up, and whether the Team's own setting is inside it
steps.description: Rule A (DES-14) over fully evaluable windows. A window holds up when its 95% forecast held in more than half of its evaluable checks, and landing above the band never counts against it. soundWindowDays is sampledWindowDays filtered, in ladder order. Determination covers the evaluated cases (AllWindowsAlike, SomeWindowsSound, NoWindowSound). The Team's own setting is Inside or Outside by membership. Read-only end to end is asserted here for the first time.
criteria: The threshold is strictly MORE than half. 2 held of 4 does not hold up; 3 of 4 does. The alternatives A′ (a strict majority of short-falls) and D (over-delivery also counts against a window) are NOT implemented. The maintainer confirmed A.
Each window is judged only on its own checks and never against another window. No per-window score is computed, stored or returned, so there is nothing a sort could use (DES-2, I1).
soundWindowDays keeps the order of sampledWindowDays. It is produced by filtering and never by sorting.
When no window holds up the answer is NoWindowSound with an empty region. Nothing names a least-bad window.
Running the check changes nothing: the Team row and its Work Items are byte-identical before and after (DoD 13).
The policy unit test adds rows for 0..4 of 4 held at 95, over-delivery in every check, and a mix of short and above-band checks.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files.
steps.implementation_notes: Only the 95% level's held flag decides a window, which is DES-14's asymmetry. The band's top edge is the median, so landing above it is a coin flip, not a finding. If a comment is needed, say that in plain words. Partly evaluable and unevaluable windows arrive at 01-06, so keep the three window states (holds up, does not, not evaluated) as the policy's internal vocabulary from now on. Commit: `feat(forecast): the region of windows that hold up, never a winner (story 6072)`

steps.name: A check that cannot be evaluated is named with its reason and counts for nothing
steps.description: Per-cell sufficiency through the shipped ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy.HasEnoughData, called unchanged on that cell's own RunChartData (TooFewActiveDays, with daysWithCompletedWork). Also the second, independent reason: the engine returned a forecast no level can be read off (DegenerateForecast, DES-9). An unevaluable cell stays in cells with forecast, actualCompleted, outcome and levelOutcomes all null, and it is excluded from every count and from the denominator.
criteria: ForecastDataSufficiencyPolicy.cs is byte-unchanged (E4, I8). MinimumActiveDays is echoed into the envelope and never re-declared. There is no second bar, and no minimum number of checks per window.

A cell the bar refuses is not sent to HowMany. A cell whose forecast is degenerate is TooFewActiveDays-independent: reason DegenerateForecast, isSufficient false. The engine's 'no reading' marker never reaches a count, a forecast value, a band or a cell (no negative number anywhere in the answer).
Every unevaluable cell is PRESENT, never omitted (I5, ADR-194), with forecast, actualCompleted, outcome and levelOutcomes null (P-D3).

runsEvaluated and scoresEvaluated count only evaluable cells, and so do heldCount and expectedHeldCount. On Coastal Survey, 12 of 16 are evaluable: the 50% level is NeverHeld at 0 of 6.0 expected, and the 95% level is SometimesHeld at 12 of 11.4.
The service unit test covers the degenerate-forecast branch and the refused-cell branch with the ports mocked.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files.
steps.implementation_notes: DES-9 says what counts as degenerate. Read ForecastBase.GetProbability and the shipped engine's sentinel for 'cannot say' before deciding the test. Do not invent a threshold of your own. If the rule is unclear from the engine, STOP and report rather than guess. Commit: `feat(forecast): a check that cannot run says why and counts for nothing (story 6072)`

steps.name: A window is judged on the checks that ran, and a window none of whose checks ran is a gap, never a pass
steps.description: The three window states now meet unevaluable checks. A partly evaluable window is judged on the checks that ran, and one check can decide it alone. A window with no evaluable check is 'not evaluated': it goes into the new unevaluatedWindowDays, never into soundWindowDays, and it turns AllWindowsAlike into SomeWindowsSound (DES-15). A not-evaluated window between two that hold up breaks the run, which the client later words as a list and not a span.
criteria: Partly evaluable: more than half of the checks that RAN must have held at 95%. Held 2 of 2 holds up, 1 of 2 does not, 1 of 1 holds up, 0 of 1 does not. No minimum number of checks per window, because that would be a second sufficiency bar, which D9 forbids.

unevaluatedWindowDays is sampledWindowDays filtered to the windows with no evaluable check, in ladder order. It never shares a member with soundWindowDays, carries no number per window, and is a subsequence of sampledWindowDays (E5(b) holds for it too).
Determination follows the DES-15 order exactly. Coastal Survey (14 not evaluated, the rest holding up) is SomeWindowsSound, never AllWindowsAlike.

The policy unit test covers every DES-14 partial case and every DES-15 branch, including the ordering tie where a window is both short and unevaluable. That cannot happen, and the test says so by construction rather than by a comment.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files.
steps.implementation_notes: The service should need no change here: the policy receives the cells and returns the region. If the service must change, the policy boundary is in the wrong place, so fix that rather than duplicating a rule in the service. Commit: `feat(forecast): a window judged on the checks that ran, a gap never a pass (story 6072)`

steps.name: When nothing could be evaluated the answer says so, and the Team's own window can be 'not determined'
steps.description: The empty end of the scale. With no evaluable check anywhere the answer is NotEnoughEvidence, every level reads NotEvaluated with heldCount 0 and expectedHeldCount 0.0, and every sampled window is listed as not evaluated. When the Team's own window is in unevaluatedWindowDays its standing is NotDetermined, and it was still tested. With nothing stored between runs, a second run over the same history answers identically.
criteria: NotDetermined means exactly one thing: the Team's own window was swept and none of its checks could be evaluated. currentSettingWasTested is true in that case and the reason is null (DES-4, DES-17 invariant).

NotEnoughEvidence comes with an empty soundWindowDays and unevaluatedWindowDays equal to sampledWindowDays. It is a first-class answer (ADR-194): the envelope is complete, with all cells present and a denominator of 0 evaluated.
Two runs on the same history produce identical envelopes. Nothing is cached in the feature, and the only caching is the metrics service's own.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files.
steps.implementation_notes: The twice-run scenario may already pass once 01-06 is green. If so, record that honestly in the commit body rather than inventing a change. It is owned here because it pins that the policy has no hidden state. Commit: `feat(forecast): nothing to conclude is an answer, and a setting can be not determined (story 6072)`

steps.name: The Team's own window is always checked — a fifth window when it is off the standard ladder
steps.description: DES-13 / I9. sampledWindowDays = sort(standard ladder ∪ {ThroughputHistory}) when the Team has a positive rolling window, which gives 20 cells when that window is off the ladder. The region can now hold a gap in either direction: the windows either side of an off-ladder setting hold up while the setting does not, or the reverse. Nothing in the answer can rank one window above another.
criteria: E5, all three parts. (a) sampledWindowDays = standardWindowDays ∪ {ThroughputHistory}, ascending and without duplicates. A Team at 14/30/60/90 still gets 16 cells. (b) soundWindowDays and unevaluatedWindowDays are subsequences of sampledWindowDays in that exact order. (c) No property anywhere in the response carries a per-window scalar, and there is no ladderKind field.
denominator.runsAttempted is 20 for an off-ladder Team. The fifth window adds four history reads and NO actual read, because the actual depends only on the horizon.

A 7-day window and a 120-day window are swept like any other; the sufficiency bar decides per check whether they can be evaluated. Non-positive windows and fixed-dates Teams are 01-09's concern and must not be added to the ladder here. If this step's union would add 0 or −7, guard it now, with 01-09 supplying the reason.
The service unit test pins the ladder composition for 14, 30, 45, 7 and 120.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green; the analyzer sweep is clean on touched files.
steps.implementation_notes: The standard ladder is echoed so the client never hard-codes it. The ladder, the horizons and the levels are static readonly arrays, never inline (CA1861). Commit: `feat(forecast): the team's own window is always one of those checked (story 6072)`

steps.name: A Team with no rolling window of its own is told its setting was not tested, and why
steps.description: DES-17. steps.description: AC-1.1's confirmation, now that the production service exists. It is a measurement, not a test. Point the [Explicit] RealityCheckWallClockProbe at the PRODUCTION ForecastRealityCheckService instead of its own copy of the sweep. Use the contract's horizons [7, 14, 28, 56] instead of the probe's [14, 28, 42, 56], and twelve samples instead of three. Measure a dev-sized Team (615 closed Work Items over 365 days) at 16 cells (window 30) and at 20 cells (window 45), cold and warm, with the query count beside each, and take the shipped single back-test on the same Team as the baseline. Record the result as budget-measurement.md in this feature's deliver folder, and fill the slice-01 brief's Measured table (DoD 8).
unskips: None — the probe stays [Explicit] (DEVOPS: a wall clock recorded on one machine says nothing on another). It is run by hand and asserts no time.
criteria: The probe constructs the production service over the real TeamMetricsService and ForecastService, at the shipped trial count. It keeps its own sweep copy nowhere, so the numbers are the product's numbers.

Twelve samples per case, cold and warm. Cases: 615 items at window 30 (16 cells) and at window 45 (20 cells). Keep the 5,000 and 20,000 volumes at window 30 as the scaling rows. Report the median and max for each case, plus the cold and warm query counts, which must read 20 and 24.
Baseline: the median and max of one shipped back-test (one HowMany plus two reads) on the same seeded Team, twelve samples.

budget-measurement.md records the machine, the commit, the trial count, the method, the table, and the verdict against the budget (median ≤ 5,000 ms, max ≤ 10,000 ms). It also says what the number is not: SQLite, in-process, one machine, no Kestrel, no load. The slice-01 brief's Measured table is filled from it, with its pending markers removed.

If the budget is MISSED: STOP and report. Do not tune the trial count or queue the work. The recorded fallback is Contingency A (read the closed items once per request), and applying it is a design decision, not part of this step.
`dotnet build` no new warning; the filtered `dotnet test` green (the probe is [Explicit] and is not selected).
steps.implementation_notes: R-1 is resolved by measurement (701 ms cold median, 16 cells, over-estimated horizons, 3 samples). This step turns that into a measurement of the contract. It runs last in the phase, as the orchestrator asked, rather than first as the DISTILL handoff suggested, and a late confirmation can no longer send the design back. The precedent's record is docs/feature/story-6053-reconstruct-over-time-history/deliver/budget-measurement.md. Rename the probe method if it now measures twenty cells too, and update the probe's summary so it no longer says it runs its own copy. phases.name: The evidence you can look at
phases.description: Story slice 02 (#6073), presentation over slice 01's response. It computes nothing and adds no backend change. Show the evidence expands one panel per sampling window swept, in ladder order: four panels, or five when the Team's own window is off the ladder. Each panel has one row per horizon, and each row draws the forecast as a band from the 95% value up to the 50% value with the four level marks and one mark at the Team's actual. Each row is normalised to its own extent and there is no shared axis across rows. An unevaluable row carries its reason in words where the band would be. Below the panels sits the nominal-rate table. The denominator and not-comparable note stay on screen whether or not the evidence is open. No charting library (DES-6).

steps.name: Each row draws the forecast as a band with its four levels and marks where the actual landed — or says in words why it could not run
steps.description: RealityCheckBandRow: one labelled group per horizon ('1 week', '2 weeks', '4 weeks', '8 weeks'). An evaluable row draws a band from the 95% value to the 50% value, four level ticks labelled 95%/85%/70%/50% and coloured by the shared helper, and one mark at the actual, labelled with its count. The row's extent is [min(value95, actual), max(value50, actual)] plus padding, so an out-of-band mark stays visible. An unevaluable row shows words where the band would be. For thin history: 'not enough history in this window', 'N days with completed Work Items, M needed'. A degenerate forecast gets its own words, and neither case shows a level label.

criteria: DES-6: plain MUI Box with positioned ticks. No @mui/x-charts, no ChartsContainer, no shared axis across rows or panels, and no new package. Every row is normalised to its own extent, because rows of different horizons are not commensurable.

E6: the row's outcome copy (CellOutcome, if it is rendered in words) and its unevaluable copy (SufficiencyReason) come through the exhaustive Record maps in realityCheckCopy.ts. The minimum is read from minimumActiveDays and the renameable terms from useTerminology().
An unevaluable row is never blank and never looks like an evaluable outcome (ADR-194). It shows no level label.

The mark's position inside the band is what reports which levels held. There is no separate per-level rendering. Where the mark sits is not asserted in jsdom; the per-theme screenshots at finalization are where it is seen.
`pnpm test` green and `pnpm build` clean with zero errors and zero warnings.
